text: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome the
Vice President of the United States, J.
D. Vance.
[applause]
Good morning. Thank you all.
Well, good morning to the press and good
morning to all the people who've worked
so hard on this. This is a great day for
American workers because we are taking
some very concrete actions to cut down
on some of the H-1B and J1 visa fraud
that we've been tracking over the past
several months. I want to give a
particular shout out to Andrew Ferguson,
Steven Miller, and of course Todd
Blanch, our great attorney general, who
are standing behind me. Uh, a particular
shout out to DO Secretary Keith
Sonderling, who's been really an amazing
partner in the anti-fraud task force.
Thanks to Keith's hard work, we've
uncovered about $20 billion dollar in
fraud just within uh his his department
and secured over 200 convictions in the
last 5 months alone. So Keith has been
one of our real allstars on the
anti-fraud task force. And of course the
IGF do Anthony Desposito all of them
will speak and then you guys can ask us
a few questions. But here here's the
basic problem something that we've been
working towards fixing in the Trump
administration for a long time. The H-1B
visa program is meant to allow companies
to bring in really the best of the best
from outside the United States of
America for positions that are
completely impossible to fill with
American workers. Unfortunately, the
program has become rife with fraud over
the last several years, probably the
last several decades. And here's the
basic game that American corporations
and foreign corporations will play. They
will say, maybe they'll put an
advertisement in a small town newspaper.
They'll go out there and say that we
have advertised for a position with our
company and nobody is responding to it.
And they will use that lack of a
response to then go and replace American
workers with what is effectively foreign
indentured servants. And I'll get into
that in a second. But these are not
people who are coming into the United
States of America, these H-1B visas,
with the full rights of an American
citizen or an American employee. They're
coming in and being mistreated by their
employers and being used to undercut the
wages of American workers. Now, there
are two ways this system fundamentally
works. The H-1B visa is how the people
get into the United States in the first
place, and then a PERM program is how
those employees stay. So, after a couple
of cycles of H-1B uh reapplication, the
the companies will then apply for a
perm, a PERM, which will allow the
employee to stay, get a green card, and
potentially stay in the United States
indefinitely. So if the H-1B visa is how
people come into the country, the PERM
program is how they stay in the United
States to begin with. Now there has been
no company in the United States
unfortunately that has abused the system
more than Microsoft. And let me just
give you a couple of statistics on this.
So in the last year, Microsoft and I
want to be clear about the data here. So
let me check this. But Microsoft laid
off last year 6,000 6,000 American
workers. At the same time, the company
benefited from 6,300 H1B visas and
almost 3,000 green cards. In other
words, if you do the math, for every
worker that Microsoft laid off, they
replaced that worker with 1 and a half
foreign indentured servants. Now, that
is a scandalous system that we've
allowed in this country for far too
long. But thanks to the work of this
task force and thanks to the empowerment
of the president of the United States,
we are going to stop it because thanks
to an ongoing investigation, we have
decided to suspend the PERM program for
Microsoft, which means they will no
longer be able to apply uh their those
they'll no longer be able to take those
H-1Bs and apply for permanent resident
status within the United States of
America. Now, our message to Microsoft
and to any other foreign or domestic
corporation is quite simple. We
obviously want you to thrive in the
United States of America. We want people
to invest in the United States of
America, particularly the American
technology sector. We are the biggest
boosters of your industry. We want you
to continue to grow and to employ a lot
of people, but we want you to employ
American workers. And so our message to
Microsoft is you're a great American
company, but you've got to hire great
American workers. You cannot lay off
American workers and then replace them
with foreign indur servants. And I want
to talk a little bit about that. When I
say indentured servants, here's what I
mean. When somebody comes in on an H-1B,
they are completely
they're completely subordinate to that
company. If they lose that job, they
have to leave the country. So if you
think of the the basic idea of an
American constitutional republic where
we bring people in who are fair and
equal citizens of the United States of
America, they are not controlled by
their employer. But you bring people in
and you basically tell them that if they
get out of line, if they get too
uppidity at work, they're not just going
to lose their job, but they're going to
be deported back to their country of
residence. Those people are not full
citizens. And that's why those people
are earning wages that are far below the
average for American citizens. The the
the second thing I want to say about
that is this fraud is facilitated not
just by the companies themselves, but in
some ways is facilitated by these
foreign outsourcing firms. These firms
that help corporations apply and find
H-1B visa candidates. They're commonly
called the witches, the four major
outsourcing firms. And these firms are
as complicit or maybe more so complicit
in the visa fraud than any American
corporation. And here is the basic data.
If you are working as an H-1B visa in
the United States of America, you're
earning $20,000 less than an American
citizen hired in the same position. If
you were brought in by one of these
foreign outsourcing firms, you're making
less than an American citizen in a
similar position. So, I'm sure that
everybody here understands the game that
is being played. You bring in indentured
servants from outside the country. You
lay off American workers. And if you're
a corporation, you make a ton of money
by undercutting the wages of American
workers, replacing them with people who
frankly shouldn't be in the United
States of America to begin with. Uh this
is a terribly pernitious system. It's
gone on for too long. And we'd all
encourage, by the way, Congress to do
something about it. But there are things
within our authority under the law, our
regulatory authority as administration
to fix this problem. And that's exactly
what we're going to do. I want to make
one final announcement here because
while we see a lot of H-1B visa fraud,
we also see a lot of J1 visa fraud. And
this is where some of America's most
elite universities bring in foreigners
again to undercut the wages of American
residents. Now, there are nine
universities in particular that we
believe merit an investigation. Those
universities are Harvard, Yale,
Stanford, Brown, the University of
Pittsburgh, UC Davis, Caltech, Arizona
State, and MIT. And what we see is that
when you employ an American worker as a
graduate student, as a researcher,
they're making about $20,000 more than
someone brought in under a J1 visa. And
importantly, these universities are
employing J1 visas for federally funded
grants at a rate of about 61%. The
national average is 38%. So something
weird is going on at these universities.
They're using these visas way too much.
They're using them to undercut the wages
of American grad students and American
researchers. and it simply has to stop.
Let me make one final point before I
turn it over to Keith. This is a
fundamental
insult to the American worker and to the
American way of life. We cannot allow
visa programs that were designed to
ensure that American corporations had
access to the best and the brightest to
use them to undercut the wages of
American workers. Now, it's one thing if
you want to bring in a person like Elon
Musk, I think 99% of American citizens
look at somebody like Elon Musk or Lisa
Sue, uh, the CEO of AMD, and they say,
obviously, if that person wants to come
in and build something great in the
United States of America, we support
that. But if you're bringing in an
accountant who's making $40,000 a year
and you use that foreign indentured
servant making $40,000 a year to replace
an American worker who was making
$70,000 a year, you're not bringing in a
genius to build a great American
corporation. You're committing fraud
against the American people and against
this visa program. It has to stop. And
thanks to the work of this task force
and again the empowerment of the
president of the United States, we are
doing something to stop it. I again
would encourage Congress to reform this
program. It is very clear that it's not
working the way that it should, but we
have tools in the administration to make
this program work better for the
American people. A lot more we could do
if Congress was willing to play ball.
And again, we extend an invitation to
both Democrats and Republicans. If you
want the H-1B visa program to stop being
used to defraud the American taxpayer
and to undercut the wages of American
workers, get to work and we will help
you. But we're going to do everything
that we can in the interimm to ensure
the program works as it was designed to
work. And with that, I want to turn it
over to our great labor secretary,
Keith. Take it away. [snorts]
